missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Конь' is a soft-stem masculine noun staying in the nominative as the predicate. 'Быстрый белый' are the agreeing masculine adjectives.
Strategic focus: Animate accusative. 'Коня' is animate masculine, so its accusative equals the genitive as the object of 'увидел'. 'Старого' agrees in the animate accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Коня' takes the genitive after 'нет' to express not having one. 'Своего' agrees in the masculine genitive.
Strategic focus: Dative recipient. 'Коню' is the dative indirect object, the one receiving the carrot from 'дала'.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Коне' is prepositional after 'на', marking the means of riding. 'Быстром' agrees in the masculine prepositional.
Strategic focus: Instrumental case. 'Конём' is instrumental after 'гордится', which governs that case. 'Своим красивым' agrees in the masculine instrumental.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Кони' is the nominative plural subject of 'паслись'. 'Дикие' is the agreeing plural adjective.
Strategic focus: Animate accusative plural. 'Коней' is animate, so the accusative plural equals the genitive plural as the object of 'кормит'. 'Своих' agrees in the animate accusative plural.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Коней' is genitive plural after 'много', counting an indefinite number.
Strategic focus: Nominative subject in a question. 'Конь' is nominative as the subject. 'Сильный' agrees in the masculine nominative, and 'чей' asks whose horse it is.
